proved_step: LEMMA R: Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= M, t real, s = |supp w| >= 1. Let S contain each coordinate independently with probability p <= 1/8, z uniform on fixed coordinates. Then P[gate [w.x >= t] non-constant in x_S] <= C_M p sqrt(n), C_M = sqrt(2)(M/2+2)+4. Proof: j = |S cap supp|, W = sum over S of |w_i| <= M j, N = s - j. Given S the gate is non-constant iff X = sum over fixed support w_i z_i lies in a half-open window of length W, so j >= 1 is needed. Case 1<=j<=s/2: N >= s/2 >= 1, all fixed weights are nonzero integers, so Erdos-Littlewood-Offord (open intervals of length 2 contain at most binom(N, floor(N/2)) sums, and binom(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N)) gives P_z <= (Mj/2+2)/sqrt(s/2). With 1[j>=1] <= j and E j = ps, this part is <= sqrt(2)(M/2+2) p sqrt(s) <= sqrt(2)(M/2+2) p sqrt(n). Case j > s/2 (s >= 2, 4p <= 1/2): P <= binom(s, ceil(s/2)) p^{ceil(s/2)} <= (4p)^{s/2} <= 4p; for s = 1 it is p. Summing gives the claim. Scope: integer weights bounded by constant M; C_M depends on M.

proved_step: LEMMA S-P1-WIN (window form of Littlewood-Offord). Let a_1..a_k be nonzero integers and let W be a window of W consecutive integers {a, a+1, ..., a+W-1}. Then #{x in {0,1}^k : sum_i a_i x_i in W} <= ceil(W/2) * C(k, floor(k/2)); equivalently Pr_x[sum_i a_i x_i in W] <= ceil(W/2) * C(k, floor(k/2)) / 2^k. Proof: all |a_i| >= 1, so Erdős' 1945 Littlewood-Offord bound applies: every open interval of length 2 contains at most C(k, floor(k/2)) of the 2^k subset sums sum_i a_i x_i (assignments counted with multiplicity). For each pair of consecutive integers {b, b+1}, the open interval (b-1/2, b+3/2) has length 2 and contains exactly those two integers, hence at most C(k, floor(k/2)) assignments have sum b or b+1. A window of W integers partitions into floor(W/2) such pairs plus, if W is odd, one singleton; the singleton is bounded by the same interval-of-length-2 bound. Summing over the pairs gives ceil(W/2) * C(k, floor(k/2)). This fixes only the window-probability term in the bounded-weight restriction bound; it does not by itself close G0001/G0004/G0007/G0009, because the restriction count k <= C m L/sqrt(n) and the weight reduction from polynomial to bounded weights remain open.

proved_step: REPAIR (random thresholds). Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= M, let c in Z be fixed, let S subset [n] contain each i independently with probability p, and let t be uniform on [-R, R] independent of S. Put mn = c + sum over i in S of min(w_i, 0) and mx = c + sum over i in S of max(w_i, 0). Claim: the gate y -> [c + sum_{i in S} w_i y_i >= t] on y in {0,1}^S is non-constant iff mn < t <= mx. Proof: the sum takes values in [mn, mx] and attains both endpoints; the gate is constant iff t <= mn (always 1) or t > mx (always 0). Given S, P_t(mn < t <= mx) <= (mx - mn)/(2R) because the interval has length mx - mn and t has density 1/(2R). Also mx - mn = sum over i in S of |w_i| <= M|S|. Taking expectation over S with E|S| = pn gives P(non-constant) <= M p n / (2R). With R = sqrt(n): P(non-constant) <= (M/2) p sqrt(n). This holds for every fixed c and every fixed x on the fixed variables, so it is an exact statement with constant M/2 and no assumption p <= 1/8.

proved_step: LEMMA (bounded integer weights, exact scope). Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= M, let N be its support, s = |N|, and let t in Z be arbitrary. Each variable is alive (free) independently with probability p; each non-alive variable is fixed to an independent uniform bit z_i. Let g(x) = [w.x >= t]. Then E[ g is non-constant over the free variables ] <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2) * p * sqrt(s) <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2) * p * sqrt(n). PROOF. Fix the alive set A, let j = |A ∩ N|, b = s - j, and let c = sum over fixed i in N of w_i z_i. Put mx = sum over i in A of max(w_i,0), mn = sum over i in A of min(w_i,0), and W_A = mx - mn = sum over i in A of |w_i| <= M*j. Zero-weight variables affect neither c nor the window. g is non-constant iff mn + c < t <= mx + c, i.e. c in [t-mx, t-mn), a half-open interval containing exactly W_A integers. Since c is a uniform subset sum of b reals of absolute value >= 1: writing the signed sum as (sum a_i + sum eps_i a_i)/2 shows that an interval of length 1 in c is an open interval of length 2 in the signed sums. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord then gives at most C(b, floor(b/2)) subsets per such interval. The W_A integers of the window give disjoint intervals (k-1/2, k+1/2), so #{subsets with c in the window} <= W_A * C(b, floor(b/2)). Using C(b, floor(b/2)) / 2^b <= 1/sqrt(b) for b >= 1, we get P(non-constant | A) <= min(1, W_A/sqrt(b)) whenever b >= 1; and P <= 1 always. AVERAGING. Case j <= s/2: then b >= s/2 >= 1 for s >= 2 (s = 1 with j = 0 has W_A = 0, probability 0). Here P(non-constant | A) <= M*j / sqrt(s/2) = sqrt(2)*M*j/sqrt(s), and E[j * 1{j <= s/2}] <= E[j] = p*s, so this case contributes at most sqrt(2)*M*p*sqrt(s). Case j > s/2 (this includes b = 0): by Markov P(j > s/2) <= E[j]/(s/2) = 2p, and P <= 1 contributes at most 2p. Summing: E <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2)*p*sqrt(s). QED. Scope: integer weights, |w_i| <= M, arbitrary threshold t, arbitrary n and p in [0,1]; the bound is per gate, so it also holds for the average over a family of gates.

proved_step: LEMMA (fixed threshold, exact scope). Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= M, t in Z fixed, S subset [n] with |S| = L, F = [n] minus S, x uniform on {0,1}^F, N = #{i in F : w_i != 0} >= 1, and l = sum over i in S of |w_i| (so l <= M L). Then P_x[ y -> [sum_{S} w_i y_i + sum_{F} w_i x_i >= t] is non-constant on {0,1}^S ] <= l / sqrt(N) <= M L / sqrt(N). PROOF. Let mx = sum_S max(w_i,0), mn = sum_S min(w_i,0), so mx - mn = l, and let c(x) = sum_F w_i x_i. The map y -> sum_S w_i y_i has min mn and max mx. Hence the function is non-constant iff mn + c < t <= mx + c, i.e. c lies in the half-open window [t - mx, t - mn), which contains exactly l integers. Zero-weight variables in F do not affect c. Let a_1..a_N be the nonzero F-weights, |a_i| >= 1. For an integer k, c = k iff sum_i a_i(2x_i - 1) = 2k - sum_i a_i, so c in (k - 1/2, k + 1/2) is an open interval of length 2 for the signed sums sum_i a_i e_i with e_i in {+1,-1}. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord gives at most C(N, floor(N/2)) sign vectors per such interval. Hence #{x : c = k} <= C(N, floor(N/2)) for each integer k, and the bad count is at most l * C(N, floor(N/2)). Dividing by 2^N and using C(N, floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N) gives P <= l/sqrt(N). QED. Scope: integer weights, |w_i| <= M, arbitrary t, L, N >= 1. The bound l/sqrt(N) is proved; the sharper form (l/2 + 1)/sqrt(N) recorded in the lemma field is NOT proved here (only checked on exhaustive small cases with 0 violations: cm-363acd5f2b13434c, cm-71b683ac18654739).
